original_question: Given a homogeneous polynomial P with integer coefficients, determine whether the equation P(x1, ..., xn) = 0 has a nonzero integer solution, meaning an integer solution different from (0, ..., 0).
target_in_paper: The closest official target is the chapter-level problem 'Existence of Non-Trivial Solutions to Homogeneous Equations' in Grechuk’s size-ordered program for Diophantine equations, i.e. identifying the smallest homogeneous equations for which the existence of a non-trivial integer solution is still unresolved.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the core mathematical object studied in the relevant part of the project: a homogeneous polynomial with integer coefficients, together with the question of whether the equation P(x1,...,xn)=0 has a non-trivial (nonzero) integer solution.
missing_details: The paper/project is not framed as an unrestricted decision problem for arbitrary input P; its actual organizing principle is to order Diophantine equations by a size parameter and study the smallest unresolved cases first.
The size parameter must be stated: for a polynomial with integer coefficients, replace each coefficient by its absolute value and evaluate the resulting polynomial at (2,...,2).
The ambient coefficient ring and solution domain should be made explicit as P in Z[x1,...,xn] and solutions in Z^n.
The paper-faithful scope is homogeneous equations within the size-ordered project, not the broad meta-problem of deciding solvability for every homogeneous polynomial.
The chapter’s mathematical context should be included: it begins with cases approachable via the Hasse principle and then moves to more advanced techniques such as the Mordell-Weil sieve.
Your draft omits the project’s emphasis on the smallest open homogeneous equations, which is the key way the question is made sharp in the paper.
No degree or family restriction is stated in the draft, whereas the paper studies explicit low-size families and examples rather than a single all-degrees theorem.
refined_question: Within Grechuk’s systematic ordering of Diophantine equations by size H(P), where for a homogeneous polynomial P in Z[x1,...,xn] the size is obtained by replacing each coefficient by its absolute value and evaluating the resulting polynomial at (2,...,2), determine the smallest homogeneous equations P(x1,...,xn)=0 for which it remains open whether there exists a non-trivial integer solution (x1,...,xn) in Z^n with (x1,...,xn) ≠ (0,...,0).
justification: The draft captures the right chapter-level predicate—existence of a non-trivial integer zero of a homogeneous polynomial—but it misses the paper’s actual framing. In this project, homogeneous equations are studied inside a systematic size-ordering of all Diophantine equations, and the goal is to isolate the smallest unresolved homogeneous instances rather than to pose a completely general decision problem for arbitrary P.
